subject: Peregrine-3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — reroute + post-incident summary
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@nimblehealth.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 2 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peregrine-3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notification

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

I wanted to let you know we're seeing an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout errors for requests served by Peregrine-3b in the us-west region starting ~08:55 PT. Our monitoring shows a rise from ~0.2% to ~4.8% error rate for short-text generation workloads; long-context chat requests are seeing more frequent timeouts.

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Traffic was partially rerouted to Peregrine-3b-ff (quantized fallback) at 09:05 PT to stabilize latency while we triage.
- Autoscaling thresholds temporarily raised for the dedicated pool serving your account.
- SREs are collecting debug traces and KV cache stats (attached sample logs).

Impact for Nimble Health: estimated 8-12% of requests during the peak window may have experienced failures or higher latency. We do not believe data was exposed beyond request-level metadata; logs are scoped to request IDs.

Next: ops will provide an update within 60–90 minutes with mitigation status. If you need us to pause routing to Peregrine-3b entirely, let me know and we can failover to an alternate model for your routes.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with the RCA and post-incident summary.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Sat, 2 Aug 2025 09:54:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Peregrine-3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notification

Mina / team — quick ops update for the thread so external folks know what we tried: 

Summary of technical findings so far:
- At ~08:52 PT a rolling increase in KV cache miss rates correlated with a surge in CPU stalls inside the attention kernels for the Peregrine-3b non-quantized path.
- The non-quantized kernel has a codepath recently changed by a runtime micropatch (deployed 2025-07-30) that alters prefetch heuristics when sequence length > 1024. We see alignment between the micropatch window and start of anomalies on some GPU instances.
- Reroute to Peregrine-3b-ff (quantized) reduced observed 5xxs by ~75% after 09:05 PT, latency normalized for most routes.

Proposed immediate mitigation:
1) Keep customer traffic on peregrine-3b-ff for 24–48 hours.
2) Roll back the prefetch heuristic change for the non-quantized kernel in the next maintenance window (low-risk revert).
3) Continue to gather traces and produce a post-incident summary.

I'll attach the abbreviated reroute playbook and logs to the customer-facing update.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
SRE, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Peregrine-3b elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer update (stabilized)

Hi Sanjay / Elena,

Quick update: we have stabilized most of the user-facing errors. Key points:
- Traffic remains routed to Peregrine-3b-ff; this reduced error rates by ~75% and restored typical P95 latency for short-span requests.
- Our SREs recommend keeping the reroute for at least 24 hours while we validate the rollback in a controlled window.
- We're preparing a brief post-incident summary (root cause, timeline, actions, and follow-up commitments) and will share a draft within 48 hours.

We appreciate the quick flag from your team — Ben will connect with Elena offline about any adjustments to your rate limits while on the fallback model.

Action requested from Nimble Health: let me know if you'd prefer we fail your traffic entirely to a different model family (we can provision that) or keep on the fallback for short-term stability.

Best,
Mina

Thanks Mina / Olga — appreciate the fast action and the context. A couple quick questions from our side: 
1) Did any request payloads get retried on our behalf in a way that could affect dedup/ordering? We use idempotency keys for critical writes.
2) Can you confirm the fallback model preserves tokenization parity for our stored prompts? We do prompt anchoring and want to avoid drift.

If the fallback is safe for tokenization, we'd prefer to keep traffic on it for 48 hours while you confirm the kernel revert. If there's any risk to semantics, please tell us and we'll accept a planned migration to a different model family.

—Sanjay

Date: Mon, 4 Aug 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Peregrine-3b — post-incident summary (draft)

Sanjay / Elena / Mina — attaching the draft summary in-line below and the full logs in the attachment for your review. We've also included the mitigation timeline and next steps.

Post-incident summary (draft):
- Incident window: 2025-08-02T08:52:00Z to 2025-08-02T11:05:00Z (peak errors 09:00–09:30 PT).
- Impact: Elevated 5xxs / timeouts for ~8–12% of Nimble Health's requests during peak; reduced to normal after reroute to Peregrine-3b-ff.
- Root cause (preliminary): A recent micropatch to the non-quantized attention prefetch heuristic introduced a path that increased CPU stalls when sequence length distributions included long (>1024) sequences; this surfaced on a subset of GPU instances with specific memory alignment patterns.
- Corrective actions taken:
  * Immediate: Traffic rerouted to quantized fallback (peregrine-3b-ff) at 09:05 PT; autoscaler thresholds adjusted.
  * Short-term: Rollback of the micropatch scheduled for 2025-08-03 02:00 PT (low-risk revert), followed by targeted verification run.
  * Long-term: Add pre-deploy synthetic tests that exercise long-sequence prefetch heuristics; expand per-instance preflight to detect alignment-sensitive kernels.
- Customer-facing commitments:
  * We will share the final post-incident report within 72 hours and the rollback verification outcome within 24 hours of the maintenance window.
  * No request payloads were retried automatically by Redwood; we did not perform any on-the-behalf retries that would affect idempotency or ordering.
  * Tokenization: The quantized fallback uses the same tokenizer and model vocabulary; we do not expect tokenization drift. We will share a short verification artifact comparing a representative sample of model outputs across the two variants.

Please review and let us know any changes you'd like before we finalize. Once we have your sign-off, we'll publish the post-incident report and mark the ticket resolved.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Platform Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
